title: Mastering Pterygium: A Clinical Guide
summary: Comprehensive overview of pterygium diagnosis, differential workup, and surgical management. This guide covers everything from clinical morphology to the complications of antimetabolite use.

sections.title: Clinical Description of Pterygium
sections.content: Colour anterior segment photograph of right eye with diffuse illumination shows Wing-shaped growth of fibrovascular tissue arising from the infero medial and infero temporal inter palpebral bulbar degenerative conjunctiva and extending onto the cornea sparing central cornea - visual axis with elevated whitish margins (“islets of Vogt”) and an iron deposition line (“Stocker”) delineating the head of the pterygium on the cornea, mild corneal haze of adjacent cornea. Visibly normal limbal architecture from 11- 1 O' clock, 5-7 O' clock (for autograft). mid dilated pupil and nuclear sclerotic cataract.

sections.title: Management Protocols
content: 1. Lifestyle: Sun, dust, and wind protection using UV-blocking sunglasses or goggles.
2. Lubrication: Artificial tears, preferably preservative-free, 4-8 times/day.

3. Inflamed Pterygium Management: Mild (Artificial tears q.i.d.); Moderate/Severe (Topical steroids: fluorometholone 0.1%/loteprednol 0.2-0.5% q.i.d.; NSAIDs: ketorolac 0.4-0.5% q.i.d.; Antihistamines/Mast cell stabilizers: bepotastine/ketotifen/olopatadine).
4. Complication Management: Use artificial tear ointment if a Dellen is present.
5. Surgical Indications: Visual axis threat, induced astigmatism, persistent irritation, contact lens interference, cosmetic concerns, or prior to cataract/refractive surgery.

sections.title: Surgical Technique Notes
content: Bare sclera technique recurrence rate: ~80% (often more aggressive).
Standard of care: Excision with conjunctival autograft (harvested from superior or upper-temporal limbal region).
Securing graft: 10-0 nylon sutures or tissue glue (e.g., TISSEEL fibrin glue).
Adjuncts: Mitomycin C or beta irradiation.
Complex cases: Peripheral lamellar keratoplasty for deep lesions.
